reading: The UN has warned that El Niño could be unusually strong.
This natural event begins in the Pacific Ocean and affects weather in other regions.
Changes in winds allow warmer water to spread eastwards and release heat into the air.
Some regions may face dry conditions, while others receive heavier rain and flooding.
It could cause disruption to economies around the world.
Countries are preparing by strengthening warning systems and arranging medical support.
The WMO is working to share forecasts with communities that may be affected.
These risks come on top of the effects of long-term global warming.
